decisive_items: Space-occupying lesion at left epidural site of T2-3 (12 × 10 × 30 mm)
Hypesthesia below chest level developed, followed by reduction in muscle strength of both lower limbs, progressing to flaccid paralysis
response.rationale: Epidural T2-3 mass with cord compression and pathologically confirmed vascular malformation best support a spinal vascular malformation. R1 adds the unsupported qualifier “arteriovenous,” while hematoma, abscess, infarction, and fistula are contradicted by the vascular pathology or lesion features.

rejected.why: Epidural hematoma is not supported by the pathological confirmation of vascular malformation; MRI signal may reflect hemorrhage but final pathology points to a vascular lesion.
Spinal cord infarction does not explain the epidural space-occupying lesion or confirmed vascular malformation.
Too nonspecific and ignores the epidural lesion and vascular pathology.
Postpartum spinal cord injury is contradicted by confirmed vascular malformation and epidural lesion.
Shares key evidence with champion but the arteriovenous qualifier is not directly supported by the vignette.
Epidural abscess is contradicted by vascular malformation and absence of infectious features.
Epidural hematoma is less supported than vascular malformation and lacks the spinal qualifier.
Spinal arteriovenous fistula is contradicted by a space-occupying epidural lesion; pathology only confirms vascular malformation.
